digest.headline: Washington and Tehran announced a ceasefire as Wall Street rebounded and the Japanese yen surged.

lede.b: Wall Street shares went up because bond yields, which are like the interest rates on government debt, stopped going up. Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire, which is a deal to stop fighting. This news made stock markets in India go up by nearly 4%. At the same time, the Japanese yen currency climbed strongly against the US dollar. In the UK, the pound currency rose slightly from a low point. Crest Nicholson, a company that builds homes, warned that it will make a loss this year because the housing market is quiet. German borrowing costs dropped slightly as market trouble eased. In China, a Zhen Ding unit invested 12 billion yuan into microchip packaging. The Reserve Bank of India took in ₹34,652 crore through a reverse repo auction, which is a way central banks take spare cash out of the banking system. Brazil's Vamos shares jumped more than 16% as investors bought cyclical stocks. Saudi Arabia saw its non-oil business activity reach a six-month high in August. Nigeria's naira currency strengthened to N1,329 per dollar.
lede.i: Wall Street broke a three-day losing streak as bond yields eased. Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire, sparking a 4% surge in Indian equity indices. The Japanese yen climbed sharply toward the 156 level against the US dollar on rate hike expectations. Sterling ticked up from a three-week low against other currencies despite falling oil prices. Crest Nicholson warned of an annual loss due to a subdued property market. German ten-year borrowing costs declined by 1.5 basis points to 3.36%. The Reserve Bank of India absorbed ₹34,652 crore via an overnight variable rate reverse repo auction. Vamos shares jumped over 16% in Brazil as capital rotated into cyclical equities. Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector reached a six-month expansion peak in August.
lede.a: The S&P 500 snapped a three-day decline as duration risk abated through falling yields. Washington and Tehran announced a bilateral ceasefire, transmitting immediate positive price action to emerging market equities like the Sensex and Nifty. The Japanese yen appreciated aggressively toward the 156 handle, pricing in tighter Bank of Japan policy and driving export-oriented domestic equities lower. Crest Nicholson issued a profit warning on lower completion volumes between 1,350 and 1,400 units. The Reserve Bank of India sterilized liquidity via a ₹34,652 crore reverse repo operation at 5.24% while zero bids cleared a ₹30,000 crore government bond buyback.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Wall Street rebounds and yields pause

stories.t: Wall Street Rallies
stories.b: The S&P 500 is an index, which is a basket of major company shares grouped together to track how the market is doing. The S&P 500 rose and snapped a three-day losing streak. Bond yields took a breather during this session. Wall Street gains helped push up Asian shares.
stories.i: The S&P 500 broke a three-day losing streak as bond yields took a breather. Wall Street gains provided positive spillover for Asian equity indices. Oil prices edged lower while the broader market recovered.
stories.a: The S&P 500 snapped its three-day losing streak alongside a pause in duration sell-offs. Lower yields created breathing room for equities, though oil prices drifted lower. Equity futures subsequently pointed higher across international venues.

stories.t: Washington and Tehran Announce Ceasefire
stories.b: Washington and Tehran announced a ceasefire agreement. Stock markets responded positively to this news. Sensex and Nifty surged nearly 4% following the announcement. Oil held steady at $95 per barrel.
stories.i: Washington and Tehran announced a ceasefire agreement. The diplomatic development prompted a strong reaction in global equities. Sensex and Nifty surged nearly 4% in response. Oil prices remained steady at $95.
stories.a: Washington and Tehran formalised a ceasefire agreement, altering geopolitical risk pricing. Sensex and Nifty surged nearly 4% on the back of the announcement. Crude benchmarks held steady at $95 per barrel despite the supply risk reduction.

politics.b: Washington announced a ceasefire agreement with Tehran. Leaders in both capitals backed the deal. Markets reacted directly to the diplomatic news.
politics.i: Washington and Tehran concluded a ceasefire agreement. The diplomatic pact altered risk premia across global markets. Regional stability measures took immediate effect.
politics.a: Washington and Tehran established a bilateral ceasefire. The agreement recalibrated Middle Eastern risk vectors, immediately impacting energy pricing and equity flows.

timeline: Washington and Tehran announce ceasefire agreement.
Wall Street snaps three-day losing streak as yields ease.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Sterling moves and Crest Nicholson issues loss warning

stories.t: Sterling Ticks Up From Three-Week Low
stories.b: Sterling is the currency used in Britain, like dollars in America. The value of sterling moved up slightly on the foreign exchange markets. It recovered from a three-week low point. This change happened as the Japanese yen went up in value. At the same time, the price of oil went down.
stories.i: Sterling edged up from a three-week low against other currencies. The currency recovered as the Japanese yen rallied across global exchanges. Meanwhile, falling oil prices altered currency dynamics. Sterling found support despite these shifting macroeconomic currents.
stories.a: Sterling bounced off a three-week low. The move coincided with a broader yen rally and cooling commodity prices in energy markets. Cross-asset correlations drove the intraday recovery in the absence of domestic tier-one data releases. The implied volatility surface adjusted as energy inputs softened.

stories.t: Crest Nicholson Warns of Annual Loss in Subdued Property Market
stories.b: Crest Nicholson is a company that builds houses for people to buy. The firm warned that it will lose money this year. The property market is very quiet right now. The company will finish building between 1,350 and 1,400 homes in the year up to 31 October. That is fewer houses than it originally expected to build.
stories.i: Crest Nicholson issued a surprise warning regarding an annual loss. The housebuilder cited a subdued property market for the difficult trading conditions. Completions for the year ending 31 October will fall between 1,350 and 1,400 units. This output trails earlier company expectations.
stories.a: Crest Nicholson flagged an unexpected full-year loss. Management pointed to depressed transaction volumes across a subdued residential property sector. Projected completions for the financial year ending 31 October were revised down to a range of 1,350 to 1,400 homes. Equity analysts must now re-evaluate inventory absorption rates for the wider housebuilding sector.

politics.b: The Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch chose a new shadow chancellor. The Guardian editorial said this choice shows a lack of insight into past election defeats. Sir Keir Starmer faced political wounds that were mostly self-inflicted.
politics.i: Kemi Badenoch appointed a new shadow chancellor. The Guardian editorial criticized the choice as lacking insight into the reasons for the Conservative party's previous election defeat. Sir Keir Starmer suffered primarily self-inflicted political damage.
politics.a: Kemi Badenoch selected a new shadow chancellor. Editorial commentary from The Guardian framed the appointment as evidence of strategic misalignment regarding the party's prior electoral defeat. Sir Keir Starmer's political vulnerability stemmed predominantly from internal missteps.

timeline: The Guardian published an editorial critiquing Kemi Badenoch's choice of shadow chancellor.
Crest Nicholson released an unscheduled trading update forecasting an annual loss.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German bond yields dip as political risks rise

stories.t: German borrowing costs drop
stories.b: Government bonds are official loans that investors buy, which pay a set return known as a yield. The yield on ten-year German bunds, which are government debt loans, fell by 1.5 basis points to 3.36%. Other European government borrowing costs dipped at the same time.
stories.i: European government bunds experienced an easing in bond market turmoil. The yield on ten-year German debt declined by 1.5 basis points to 3.36%. French ten-year bond yields moved lower by 1.5 basis points to 4.23% concurrently.
stories.a: Ten-year German bund yields compressed by 1.5 basis points to print at 3.36% amid a broader cooling of European sovereign debt volatility. French ten-year yields mirrored this downward trajectory, declining by 1.5 basis points to 4.23%.

politics.b: Christian Democrats avoid campaigning with the German chancellor. They try to slow the rise of the far right in Saxony-Anhalt. Friedrich Merz becomes a liability as the Alternative for Germany surges.
politics.i: Christian Democrats bypass campaigning with the German chancellor. The party attempts to slow the rise of the far right in Saxony-Anhalt. Friedrich Merz emerges as a liability as the AfD surges.
politics.a: Christian Democrats eschew joint campaigning with the German chancellor to mitigate electoral damage in Saxony-Anhalt. Friedrich Merz constitutes a political liability as the AfD sustains its electoral surge.

timeline: The yield on 10-year German bunds falls 1.5bps to 3.36%.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen surges on rate hike and intervention expectations

stories.t: Japanese Yen Surges on Rate Hike Expectations
stories.src: The Guardian · Investing.com · 富途牛牛
stories.b: The Japanese yen is a kind of money used in Japan. It just went up in value very quickly for two days in a row. Traders think the Bank of Japan, which is the country's central bank that controls money rules, will raise interest rates soon. Interest rates are like the cost of borrowing money. The currency reached the 156 level against the US dollar.
stories.i: The Japanese yen climbed sharply for two consecutive sessions, retesting the 156 level against the US dollar. Market participants anticipate that the Bank of Japan will tighten monetary policy by raising borrowing costs. This shift follows warnings from a Japanese currency diplomat regarding ongoing market concerns over exchange rates.
stories.a: The Japanese yen appreciated across two consecutive sessions, testing the 156 threshold against the US dollar. Speculation regarding a Bank of Japan policy rate hike catalyzed the move alongside verbal warnings from domestic currency diplomats. Market participants continue to price in potential carry trade unwinding as policy divergence narrows.

stories.t: Nikkei Falls for Fourth Session
stories.b: The Nikkei is a stock market index, which is a group of shares from big companies in Japan put together to track how the market is doing. It went down for the fourth day in a row. It reached its lowest level recently. This drop happened while the local currency got stronger against the dollar.
stories.i: The Nikkei index extended its losing streak to a fourth consecutive session, hitting its lowest level. Japanese equities faced downward pressure as the strengthening local currency weighed on sentiment. Currency movements often impact domestic exporters whose foreign earnings convert back at lower rates.
stories.a: The Nikkei equity index registered its fourth consecutive decline, touching a local trough. Domestic share prices dropped as the appreciating local currency compressed margins for export-heavy constituents. The concurrent rally in the exchange rate created strong headwinds for local equities.

politics.b: Government officials in Japan talked about the currency markets. A currency diplomat warned about ongoing issues with the yen. Authorities kept watch on the foreign exchange rates.
politics.i: Japanese currency diplomats issued warnings regarding ongoing foreign exchange market concerns. Authorities maintained verbal pressure amid sharp currency fluctuations. The official stance emphasized vigilance over speculative moves in the foreign exchange market.
politics.a: Japanese currency authorities escalated verbal interventions through explicit warnings regarding exchange rate volatility. Diplomatic messaging sought to deter speculative short positions in the local currency. Officials refrained from confirming direct market operations while maintaining high alert status.

timeline: The Japanese yen retests the 156 level against the US dollar amid intervention threats.
The Nikkei stock index falls for the fourth straight session to hit its lowest level.

China.label: China
China.sub: Land auctions diverge, sports industry targets and tech investment

stories.t: Zhen Ding Unit Allocates 12 Billion Yuan for Packaging Substrate Base
stories.b: Zhen Ding Technology has a unit that puts money into building things. This unit will spend 12 billion yuan to make an advanced packaging substrate base. A substrate base is a foundational layer used for holding tiny computer chips. Big companies build these to help manufacture better electronics.
stories.i: A Zhen Ding Technology unit will invest 12 billion yuan in an advanced packaging substrate base. This capital expenditure targets microchip manufacturing infrastructure. The deployment expands production capacity for high-end semiconductor components.
stories.a: Zhen Ding Technology's subsidiary commits 12 billion yuan to an advanced packaging substrate base. This outlay scales high-density interconnect infrastructure within the semiconductor supply chain. The capital deployment implies sustained domestic demand for domestic advanced node packaging capabilities.

stories.t: Beijing Land Auction Shows Divergence While Sports Sector Eyes Growth
stories.src: finance.biggo.com · Global Times · 巴士的報
stories.b: Beijing held its first land auction under a new policy. The Jiangtai plot was stopped before bidding started. Meanwhile, a residential site in Shunyi drew 170 rounds of bids. Officials also announced a goal for the sports industry to reach over 7 trillion yuan by 2030.
stories.i: Beijing hosted its first land auction under a new policy, yielding stark divergence. The Jiangtai plot was suspended before bidding commenced. Conversely, a residential site in Shunyi attracted 170 rounds of bidding. Separately, officials targeted a sports industry valuation exceeding 7 trillion yuan by 2030 while moving to suppress toxic fan-circle culture.
stories.a: Beijing's inaugural land auction under the new policy demonstrated bifurcation, evidenced by the pre-bidding suspension of the Jiangtai plot alongside 170 competitive rounds for the Shunyi residential site. Concurrently, state planners set a 2030 target for the sports industry to exceed 7 trillion yuan. This commercial target is paired with regulatory crackdowns on toxic fan-circle culture.

stories.t: Summer Box Office Reaches 12.5 Billion Yuan as Film Industry Faces Losses
stories.b: China's box office for the summer hit 12.5 billion yuan and kept its growth momentum. At the same time, 70% of film and television companies face loss-making growing pains. Many firms wonder if AI transformation is a lifeline for survival.
stories.i: China's summer box office recorded 12.5 billion yuan, sustaining growth momentum. Despite this theater revenue, 70% of film and television companies face loss-making growing pains. Industry participants now question whether artificial intelligence transformation will serve as a lifeline for survival.
stories.a: China's summer box office aggregated 12.5 billion yuan to maintain sector growth momentum. However, structural headwinds persist as 70% of listed film and television companies report loss-making growing pains. Corporate survival strategies increasingly center on whether artificial intelligence transformation can rescue compressed margins.

politics.b: China rejected G20 trade-imbalance claims. Officials stated there is no need to devalue the yuan.
politics.i: China rejected G20 trade-imbalance claims. Officials asserted that no need exists to devalue the yuan.
politics.a: Beijing formally rejected G20 trade-imbalance claims. Authorities maintained that domestic fundamentals preclude any need to devalue the yuan.

timeline: China rejects G20 trade-imbalance claims and states no need to devalue the yuan.
Beijing holds its first land auction under a new policy with mixed results across plots.
Zhen Ding Technology unit announces a 12 billion yuan investment in an advanced packaging substrate base.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity auctions, rupee gains, and equity market moves

stories.t: Central Bank Absorbs Cash Via Reverse Repo As Rupee Extends Advance
stories.src: Reserve Bank of India · Business Standard
stories.b: The central bank asked commercial banks to lock away ₹3,50,000 crore total in two separate reverse repo auctions, offering a 5.24% return for one day. A reverse repo is when banks lend spare cash to the central bank for a short time, which removes money from the broader economy. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee strengthened against other currencies for the fifth day in a row. At the same time, the central bank received no bids to buy back its older dated securities from the market.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India accepted ₹34,652 crore through its second overnight variable rate reverse repo auction at a weighted average rate of 5.24%. This liquidity withdrawal operation coincided with the Indian rupee extending its winning streak to a fifth consecutive session. Concurrently, a scheduled buyback auction for government securities totaling ₹30,000 crore in face value attracted zero accepted offers.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India drained liquidity via a secondary 1-day variable rate reverse repo clearing at 5.24% for ₹34,652 crore after earlier absorption attempts. Concurrently, the INR appreciation channel remained active as the currency notched a fifth successive daily advance. In sovereign debt management, a ₹30,000 crore face value buyback auction yielded zero accepted bids across multiple dated tenors.

stories.t: Equities Fall As Closing Auction Rule Changes Lift Options Costs
stories.src: DT Next · TradingView · Reserve Bank of India
stories.b: Stock markets dropped for the fourth day in a row, with the Sensex falling 417 points due to rising crude oil prices and a sell-off in technology shares. A new closing auction format caused options premiums on the Sensex to jump by 500%. Meanwhile, the central bank prepared a fresh underwriting auction for ₹32,000 crore of government securities.
stories.i: Domestic equity indices extended their losing streak to four sessions as the Sensex slid 417 points amid an information technology sell-off and rising crude prices. Structural changes to the market closing auction drove Sensex options premiums up by 500%. Meanwhile, the central bank announced a ₹32,000 crore government security underwriting auction scheduled for the following day.
stories.a: Equities sustained a four-session drawdown as the Sensex retreated 417 points under pressure from tech sector liquidations and higher crude inputs. Implementation of a revised closing auction mechanism induced a 500% expansion in Sensex options premiums. Concurrently, authorities readied a ₹32,000 crore sovereign debt issuance requiring institutional underwriting commitments.

politics.b: No political events were reported in the financial updates today.
politics.i: No political updates or legislative announcements appeared in the session data.
politics.a: No political or regulatory policy shifts outside of central bank operations were documented.

timeline: Extant scheme of underwriting commitment notified by authorities
Reserve Bank of India holds overnight variable rate reverse repo auction
Government security buyback auction records zero accepted offers
Underwriting auction scheduled for ₹32,000 crore government securities sale

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Braskem credit line and stock movements in Brazil

stories.t: Braskem secures Petrobras credit line
stories.b: Braskem secured a credit line worth R$ 2.35 billion from Petrobras. A credit line is like an agreed limit on a loan that a company can draw from when it needs money. Braskem will use these funds specifically for purchasing feedstock, which is the raw material used in manufacturing. This financial backing was finalized on September 2.
stories.i: Braskem obtained a R$ 2.35 billion credit line from Petrobras. The firm will deploy this liquidity for feedstock procurement. This transaction was reported on September 2.
stories.a: Braskem secured a R$ 2.35 billion credit facility from Petrobras to finance feedstock acquisitions. The capital injection provides balance sheet flexibility for raw material inventory management. The transaction was disclosed on September 2.

stories.t: Vamos shares jump as investors shift to cyclicals
stories.b: Vamos saw its stock price jump by over 16 percent. Shares represent tiny pieces of ownership in a business, bought and sold on a public market. Investors moved their money into Brazilian cyclical stocks, which are companies whose fortunes rise and fall closely with the health of the wider economy. This market movement occurred on September 3.
stories.i: Vamos equity surged over 16 percent. Market participants rotated capital into domestic cyclical shares, which track economic expansions and contractions. This price action was recorded on September 3.
stories.a: Vamos equities rallied over 16 percent amid a broader sector rotation into Brazilian cyclicals. Market participants reallocated duration and risk exposure toward economically sensitive equities. The repricing materialized on September 3.

politics.b: Brazil's financial markets rallied recently. This came as an election poll tightened. Investors reacted to the shifting political figures on September 2.
politics.i: Brazilian markets experienced a rally driven by tightening election polls. Asset prices responded to the political shift on September 2.
politics.a: Brazilian asset prices rallied following the publication of a tighter election poll on September 2. Market valuations adjusted to the shifting political probabilities.

timeline: Brazil's markets rallied as an election poll tightened
Braskem secured a R$ 2.35 billion credit line from Petrobras

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Saudi non-oil sector growth and corporate deals

stories.t: Non-Oil Sector Expansion Reaches Six-Month Peak
stories.b: Saudi Arabia saw its non-oil private sector grow at the fastest pace in six months during August. Non-oil means businesses that do not sell crude petroleum. This index tracks business activity like manufacturing and services. The reading hit a six-month high in August.
stories.i: The Saudi non-oil private sector accelerated to a six-month high in August. Business activity expanded across manufacturing and services. This metric tracks non-oil economic momentum. The August survey captured this peak.
stories.a: Saudi non-oil private sector growth printed a six-month high in August. Momentum in non-oil verticals expanded against broader commodity headwinds. The survey data implies resilient domestic demand independent of hydrocarbon output. August figures confirmed the rate of expansion.

stories.t: Aramco Expands Partnerships and Venture Capital Deployments
stories.b: Saudi Aramco signed new deals with French firms like SLB, Vallourec, and Dassault to court French investment. Aramco Digital also joined with Avathon to use industrial artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, Wa’ed Ventures, which is Aramco's venture capital arm, invested in COFE Tech before its initial public offering. An initial public offering means a company is selling shares to the public for the first time.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco signed agreements with SLB, Vallourec, and Dassault to build French investment ties. Aramco Digital partnered with Avathon to deploy industrial artificial intelligence. Separately, Wa’ed Ventures injected capital into COFE Tech ahead of its initial public offering.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco executed partnership agreements with SLB, Vallourec, and Dassault to channel French industrial investment. Aramco Digital integrated Avathon for industrial artificial intelligence adoption. Wa’ed Ventures deployed capital into COFE Tech ahead of its initial public offering, pricing private equity prior to public markets.

politics.b: Saudi energy firms looked at bonded storage sites in Pakistan alongside Kuwait Petroleum, Vitol, and Trafigura. Iraq also stated aims to double its oil production capacity to 10 million barrels per day. Aramco and other firms eyed these Pakistan storage options on September 3. Iraq announced its production goals on the exact same date.
politics.i: Saudi Aramco joined Kuwait Petroleum, Vitol, and Trafigura in evaluating bonded storage opportunities in Pakistan. Iraq stated a target to double its crude capacity to 10 mbpd. Officials confirmed these developments on September 3.
politics.a: Saudi entities evaluated Pakistani bonded storage infrastructure alongside Kuwait Petroleum, Vitol, and Trafigura. Iraq articulated a capacity target of 10 mbpd, altering regional supply projections. Officials confirmed these strategic positioning moves on September 3.

timeline: Visual Capitalist released global crude oil producer rankings for 2025.
Aramco Digital and Avathon announced an artificial intelligence partnership.
Saudi non-oil private sector growth reached a six-month high in August data.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira rally, treasury bill yields, and economic activity

stories.t: Naira Extends Rally Against Dollar on Foreign Exchange Inflows
stories.src: Brand Icon Image · GuruFocus · MarketForces Africa
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. It gained value against the US dollar. The exchange rate reached N1,329 per dollar. Strong foreign exchange inflows helped push the naira up. Higher oil prices and increased remittances also supported the currency.
stories.i: The naira strengthened to N1,329 per dollar on September 3, 2026. This rally was driven by robust foreign exchange inflows. Rising global oil prices and increased remittance flows supported the currency gain. The official rate closed at N1,329 to the USD.
stories.a: The official USD/NGN rate closed at N1,329, extending the currency's recent appreciation. FX inflows, alongside supportive terms of trade from higher crude oil prices and steady remittance channels, drove the spot convergence. The broader question is whether reserve accumulation matches the pace of these inflows.

stories.t: Central Bank of Nigeria Lowers Treasury Bill Yields Below 17 Percent
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria is the main bank that runs the country's money system. It lowered treasury bill yields to 16.8 percent. Yields are the money made on short-term government debt, like interest paid to people who lend money to the government. This is the lowest level since June 3.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its treasury bill yields to 16.8 percent on September 3, 2026. This drop pushed yields below the 17 percent threshold. This rate represents the lowest yield observed since June 3. Lower yields reduce the returns paid to investors holding short-term government paper.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Nigeria reduced benchmark treasury bill yields to 16.8%, marking the lowest level since June 3. This adjustment in short-term sovereign paper yields reflects shifting domestic liquidity conditions. Fixed-income portfolio managers must reprice short duration assets following this sub-17% print.

stories.t: Nigeria Economic Activity Expands for Third Consecutive Month
stories.b: Economic activity in Nigeria grew for the third month in a row. The composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 52.7. This index measures how busy factories and businesses are. A number above 50 means the economy is growing.
stories.i: Nigeria's composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 52.7 in September 2026. This increase marks the third consecutive month of economic expansion. The index tracks business conditions, with readings above 50 signalling growth.
stories.a: The composite Purchasing Managers' Index printed at 52.7, confirming a third consecutive month of expansionary economic activity. This survey metric points to sustained demand across private sector operators. The continued reading above the 50 expansion threshold validates current output momentum.

politics.b: Police officials gave out 2.3 billion naira in insurance money to families of officers who died. Meanwhile, criminals demanded 40 million naira from Kebbe town in a security crisis.
politics.i: Inspector-General of Police Disu distributed 2.3 billion naira in insurance cheques to beneficiaries of fallen police officers. Separately, bandits demanded 40 million naira from Kebbe town amid an ongoing security crisis in Sokoto.
politics.a: IGP Disu disbursed 2.3 billion naira in welfare payouts to dependents of deceased police personnel. Concurrently, security operations faced persistent strain as bandits demanded a 40 million naira ransom from Kebbe town in Sokoto.

timeline: Treasury bill yields previously touched levels last seen before the recent rise.
Naira reaches N1,329 per dollar and composite PMI rises to 52.7.
